scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Umxhentso is rooted in the traditions of the Xhosa people, particularly in the Transkei homeland of the Eastern Cape.
It has historically served as a vital component of Xhosa ceremonies, ranging from healing rituals to rites of passage.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Umxhentso is used in healing ceremonies by Amagqirha, weddings (Umdudo), and rites of passage such as Ulwaluko (Umguyo).
It is a source of pride and cultural identity for the Xhosa people.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is provided by the Uhadi musical bow, drums, and the Impempe whistle made from Ingcongolo reed.
Vocal accompaniment, known as ukombela, involves theme songs and rhythmic clapping.
Listen for the Uhadi musical bow, Drum, Impempe whistle (Ingcongolo reed).
The music is characterized by the resonance of the Uhadi bow, the percussive strike of drums, the sharp tone of the reed whistle, and vocal theme songs accompanied by clapping.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wear umbhaco, which are traditional beaded garments.
Dancers often apply paint to their bodies before performing.
The dance is frequently performed in the Transkei region of the Eastern Cape.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variants include Umngqungqo (ancient, dignified, for older women), Umdudo (wedding dance with spinning), Intlombe (for healers' initiation), and Umguyo (boys' initiation).

narration: Umxhentso is variant of Umngqungqo: A dignified, slow dance for older women in ritual ceremonies.
Umxhentso is variant of Umdudo: A wedding dance involving spinning movements.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Umxhentso is used in initiation and healing ceremonies by Amagqirha; outsiders should respect the ritual nature of these performances.
